title: SWINGLIGHT / LIVING FUNCTION
core_formula: reclaimed materials -> functional anatomy -> recognizable character -> micro-story -> useful collectible object
secondary_lesson: BUILD A MICRO-STORY INTO THE OBJECT.
summary: A desk lamp becomes a swing scene where the bulb is the head, the socket is the torso, bent metal becomes the body, reclaimed wood becomes the frame, and the object reads as both a light and a tiny character.
learn: Ask whether a function can be imagined as a creature.
Anthropomorphism should emerge from function rather than be pasted on top.
Functional components can become anatomy and narrative.
Micro-stories can make objects emotionally memorable.
Natural motion can be stronger than electronics.
Every material should have a job in the story.
avoid: Edison bulb as mandatory bulb choice
two wood posts and rope as fixed recipe
failure_modes: decorative character added beside an ordinary lamp instead of emerging from the lamp function
lamp and character read as two independent objects
unnecessary decorative parts do not serve anatomy, structure, light, or narrative
source: user-provided concept text + 3 images for CONCEPT 06
